identity.title: Unlocking State-Tracking in Linear RNNs Through Negative Eigenvalues

problem.claim: The paper addresses state-tracking in efficient recurrent architectures, including solving parity and counting modulo 3.

gap.claim: Prior analysis linked LRNN parity failure to restricting diagonal transition values to [0,1], but the authors identify an unresolved extension to non-diagonal LRNNs such as DeltaNet.

contributions.claim: Proves that finite-precision LRNNs with only positive transition-matrix eigenvalues cannot solve parity, and that non-triangular matrices are needed to count modulo 3.
Proves that LRNNs can learn any regular language when transitions are products of identity-minus-vector-outer-product matrices with eigenvalues in [-1,1].
Extends the transition-eigenvalue range of Mamba and DeltaNet to include negative values and evaluates the resulting state-tracking and scaled pretraining behavior.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that their analysis extends the negative-eigenvalue result from diagonal LRNNs to non-diagonal architectures and provides broader theoretical characterization of state-tracking.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that Mamba and DeltaNet with negative eigenvalues solve parity and consistently improve performance on state-tracking tasks.
The authors report stable, efficient pretraining of state-tracking-enabled LRNNs at 1.3B parameters, with competitive language-modeling performance and promise on code and math tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: LRNNs are presented as efficient alternatives to Transformers for long sequences.
Transformers and LRNNs struggle with state-tracking; even parity is unsolved by current architectures in one forward pass.
Earlier work attributed LRNN parity failure to diagonal transition values restricted to [0,1] and reported that negative values resolve it.
This paper extends the result to non-diagonal LRNNs and gives impossibility and regular-language learnability results.
Experiments report improved state tracking and stable large-scale pretraining with competitive language modeling results.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects an observed failure on parity to a specific architectural constraint—the allowed eigenvalue range—and then tests that targeted modification across architectures.

lessons.interpretation: A narrowly defined failure case can motivate a mechanistic intervention and a focused cross-architecture evaluation.
lessons.application: When presenting a new architecture, identify a minimal diagnostic task, state the suspected constraint, and evaluate the corresponding intervention on more than one model family.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the diagnostic task is not representative of the intended deployment setting or the suspected mechanism is not independently supported.

source_observation.claim: The paper separates finite-precision impossibility results, modulo-counting structural requirements, and a constructive regular-language result.

lessons.interpretation: Separating theorem scopes and assumptions helps prevent broad capability claims from being inferred from one result.
lessons.application: Organize theoretical claims by task class, matrix structure, and precision assumptions before relating them to empirical behavior.
lessons.exception: This level of decomposition may be unnecessary for a paper whose contribution is purely empirical and has no distinct theoretical regimes.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the experimental benchmarks, baselines, effect sizes, or statistical variability behind the reported improvements and competitiveness.
It does not state the precise finite-precision model or the conditions and construction details for the regular-language theorem.
The meaning of “promise” on code and math tasks is not quantified.
